Line 3: 'Mỗi sprint dài hai tuần.' Hence 4-5 sprints = 8-10 weeks and (try-it) 3-4 sprints = 6-8 weeks.

WebFetch https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html (R2): 'the more the Developers know about their past performance, their upcoming capacity, and their Definition of Done, the more confident they will be'. Sec 4 now carries all three items and states the gloss as a separate sentence of its own ('Upcoming capacity means how much they can work in the coming sprint'), not attributed to the Guide. Round-1 minor resolved.

No pinned source covers velocity ranges: the 2020 Guide has 0 hits for 'velocity' and names only 'burn-downs, burn-ups, or cumulative flows' as forecasting practices. It does support the basis ('Only what has already happened may be used for forward-looking decision making'), and the repo data (8-11) supports the variation argument. Kind opinion, stated with its reason; no blocker.

First half is consistent with the Guide's Topic Two sentence (upcoming capacity informs how much is selected). 'Redone at every sprint planning' and 'turns into a promise' have no pinned source (Guide: no 'remaining', no release forecast cadence); they match velocity-history.md lines 41-43. Kind opinion, no absolutes; no blocker.

issues.quote: the product owner, who decides what the team builds next
issues.text: Overstates the role for the pinned Guide. Scrum Guide 2020: the Product Owner is accountable for 'Ordering Product Backlog items', while in Sprint Planning 'the Developers select items from the Product Backlog to include in the current Sprint'. The PO orders the work; the Developers choose what goes into the sprint. The lesson itself says the team 'takes in' points (sec 4, 5).
issues.fix: Replace with: "the product owner, who decides the order of the work the team builds".

issues.quote: Scale the low and the high down roughly in line with the share of the usual work people can do.
issues.text: Round-1 gap is fixed (section 4 now says how much less, section 5 shows 8 × ¾ = 6 and 11 × ¾ ≈ 8). But I first read 'the usual work people' as one noun and had to re-read the sentence to get 'the share of the usual work that the available people can do'.
issues.fix: Reword to: 'Scale the low and the high down roughly by the share of the usual work the available people can do, for example three quarters when three of four are available.'

issues.quote: the team takes in, meaning plans into the sprint, less than its usual velocity, instead of expecting the others to cover the gap
issues.text: The meaning of 'take in' is now given (round-1 issue resolved), but the gloss set off by commas splits 'takes in … less than' and the sentence has four comma parts; I re-read it once.
issues.fix: Put the gloss in its own sentence right after: '… the team takes in less than its usual velocity, instead of expecting the others to cover the gap. To take in points means to plan them into the sprint.'
